name: Saltgrave Denim Chore Coat
description:
A four-pocket chore coat in 14oz raw indigo denim, cut boxy and slightly long in a French workwear tradition. The construction is triple-stitched throughout in gold thread, with bartacks at every stress point and a lining of natural cotton twill that breathes better than most tech fabrics. Saltgrave is a small independent label — two people, a press, and a roster of specialty fabric suppliers — making a handful of pieces per run that sell out in days through their direct channel.

This jacket has no branding visible from the outside. If you know Saltgrave, you recognize the distinctive pocket placement and the custom shank buttons. If you don't, it just looks like a very well-made denim jacket worn by someone who has good taste and doesn't announce it. It fades spectacularly with wear — the creases go white, the body deepens, and after a year it looks like something that cost three times as much.
what_it_says: You know things about clothing that most people don't. You found this without being told to find it. That matters to you.
story_hooks: The two founders of Saltgrave have gone silent — their direct channel is dark, the last run was never shipped, and the people who pre-ordered are getting increasingly worried about more than their money.
A Saltgrave chore coat appears in an archival photo from 2187 — thirteen years before the brand was founded — worn by someone who looks identical to one of its current owners.

A limited run of Saltgrave coats was dyed using indigo from a specific urban farm in the Shelf district; that farm has since been razed, and someone is willing to pay extraordinary amounts for any piece from that batch.

physical_description.visual_profile: A boxy, slightly oversized four-pocket chore coat with a deliberate vintage workwear silhouette. The cut sits square on the shoulders and falls past the hip, creating a relaxed, utilitarian presence that reads as deliberately understated luxury.
physical_description.fit: Boxy and intentionally roomy through the chest and shoulders; slightly long in the body with straight-cut sleeves. Designed for layering and movement, not tailored to the frame.
physical_description.primary_material: 14oz raw indigo denim — dense, stiff when new, breaks in with character. Natural cotton twill lining throughout.
physical_description.texture: Densely woven, rigid denim surface with visible selvage; gold triple-stitching creates fine linear texture at seams. Lining is soft brushed cotton. Brass shank buttons catch light subtly.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep raw indigo that will fade dramatically with wear — creases will show bright white against the indigo. Warm gold stitching throughout provides subtle contrast. Buttons are darkened brass.
physical_description.closures: Five custom brass shank buttons down the front; two chest patch pockets with bartacked corners, two lower pockets with reinforced stress points.
distinctive_features: Triple-stitched seams in gold thread throughout entire garment
Bartacks at all stress points (pocket corners, button bases, underarm seams)
Distinctive off-center pocket placement (Saltgrave signature detail)
Natural cotton twill lining breathes better than synthetic alternatives
Completely unmarked exterior — no visible branding or labels
Fades spectacularly with wear — signature feature of the piece
French workwear construction tradition evident in cut and proportions
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 crossover: independently manufactured luxury positioned as anti-conspicuous. Price point suggests Tier 2 wealth, but aesthetic appeal reaches Tier 3 working class who recognize quality.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearer signals refined taste, connection to analog craftsmanship, and rejection of corp-logo visibility. Worn by makers, engineers, architects, and anyone in GLMZ who values durability over status display. No augmentation required to appreciate this piece.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when new (stiff, deep indigo), then evolves into broken-in character piece. Creases develop white lines; hems and cuffs soften; overall patina deepens. A year of wear transforms it into a personal artifact.
